At AWI Management Corp., we believe property management is about more than buildings—it’s about the people who live in them and the communities we create.



We deliver exceptional, mission\-driven property management that drives long\-term success for property owners while providing quality housing for residents.



We are seeking an experienced and compassionate PSH Program Manager to support Permanent Supportive Housing (PSH) operations across a 750\-unit portfolio consisting of six properties throughout California’s Central Valley.



This is a specialized leadership role designed to support the unique operational demands of Permanent Supportive Housing communities serving individuals and families exiting homelessness, including residents living with serious mental illness, trauma histories, and substance use disorders.



The PSH Program Manager partners closely with Regional Management leadership and serves as AWI’s portfolio\-level subject matter expert for Housing First implementation, housing retention strategy, service provider coordination, staff training, and PSH operational support.

Join the dynamic journey at Vynca, where we're passionate about transforming care for individuals with complex needs.  

  

We’re more than just a team; we're a close\-knit community. Our shared commitment to caring for each other and those we serve is what sets us apart. Guided by our unwavering core values: Excellence, Compassion, Curiosity, and Integrity, we forge paths of success together. Join us in this transformative movement where you can contribute to making a profound difference every day.  

  

At Vynca, our mission is to provide comprehensive care for more quality days at home.

**About the job**
=================

*Internal Title: Clinical Lead Care Manager*


We are looking for a highly skilled Clinical Lead Care Manager (CLCM) to join our team serving Sacramento County, CA. Reporting to the ECM Clinical Manager, the CLCM acts as the client’s primary point of contact, partnering with healthcare providers and support services to ensure coordinated, aligned, and comprehensive care.The CLCM manages client cases, coordinates health care benefits, provides education and facilitates member access to care in a timely and cost\-effective manner. The CLCM collaborates and communicates with the client’s caregivers/family support persons, other providers, and others in the Care Team to promote wellness, recovery, independence, resilience, and member empowerment, while ensuring access to appropriate services and maximizing member benefit.

***This is a hybrid position that requires traveling throughout the Sacramento County area up to 5 days per week. Candidates wishing to be considered must reside within 25\-miles of the assigned territory due to frequency of travel.***

*This is a critical role and we're looking to fill it as soon as possible.*

**What you’ll do**
==================

*Hybrid (in\-person and remote) care management duties as described below:*

* Assess member needs in the areas of physical health, mental health, SUD, oral health, palliative care, memory care, trauma\-informed care, social supports, housing, and referral and linkage to community\-based services and supports
* Oversees the development of the client care plans and goal settings
* Offer services where the member resides, seeks care, or finds most easily accessible, including office\-based, telehealth, or field\-based services
* Connect clients to other social services and supports that are needed
* Advocate on behalf of the client with health care professionals (e.g. PCP, etc.)
* Utilize evidence\-based practices, such as Motivational Interviewing, Harm Reduction, and Trauma\-Informed Care principles
* Conduct outreach and engagement activities in order to facilitate linkage to the ECM program and log activity in the Client Relationship Management (CRM) system
* Evaluate client’s progress and update SMART goals
* Provide mental health promotion
* Arrange transportation (e.g., ACCESS)
* Complete all documentation, including outcome measures within the timeframes established by the individual care plans
* Maintain up\-to\-date patient health records in the Electronic Medical Record (EMR) system and other business systems
* Complete monthly reporting to ensure program compliance
* Attend training as assigned

**Your experience \& qualifications**
=====================================

* ACSW, LPCC, LCSW, or LMFT license in California required
* 1\+ year of experience as a care manager, care navigator, or community health worker supporting vulnerable populations. *2 or more years preferred.*
* Willing and able to work Monday\-Friday 8:30am\-5:00pm, both in the field and remotely, with flexibility for potential evenings and weekends.
* Working knowledge of government and community resources related to social determinants of health
* Excellent oral and written communication skills
* Positive interpersonal skills required
* Clean driving record, valid driver's license, and reliable transportation
* Must have general computer skills and a working knowledge of Google Workspace, MS Office, and the internet
* Bilingual (English/Spanish) *preferred*

**Additional Information**
--------------------------

* The hiring process for this role may consist of applying, followed by a phone screen, online assessment(s), interview(s), an offer, and background/reference checks.
* Background Screening: A background check, which may include a drug test or other health screenings depending on the role, will be required prior to employment.
* Job Description Scope: This job description is not exhaustive and may include additional activities, duties, and responsibilities not listed herein.
* Vaccination Requirement: Employees in patient, client, or customer\-facing roles must be vaccinated against influenza. Requests for religious or medical accommodations will be considered but may not always be approved.
* Employment Eligibility: Compliance with federal law requires identity and work eligibility verification using E\-Verify upon hire.
* Equal Opportunity Employer: At Vynca Inc., we embrace diversity and are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace. We value all applicants regardless of race, color, religion, age, national origin, ancestry, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, veteran status, disability, genetic information, citizenship status, or membership in any other protected group under federal, state, or local law.

**Location:** San Francisco, CA; 5 days in office/week

**Status:** Full time; non\-exempt (40 hours/week FT NE)

**Salary:** $62,000 \- $67,000/year

**Reports to:** Housing Director, Co\-Executive Director

**Organization Description**

The Miss Major Alexander L. Lee TGIJP Black Trans Cultural Center is a team of transgender, gender\-variant and intersex people, inside and outside of prisons, jails, detention centers, and other locked facilities creating a united family in the struggle for survival and freedom. We work in collaboration with others to forge a culture of resistance and resilience to strengthen us for the fight against human rights abuses, imprisonment, police violence, racism, poverty, and societal pressures. We seek to create a world rooted in self\-determination, freedom of expression, and gender justice.

**Position Description**

Housing Case Managers at TGIJP are expected to provide comprehensive case management services to clients experiencing housing insecurity or homelessness. This role involves assessing client needs, developing housing plans, advocating for client rights, and connecting clients with appropriate resources and services. Housing Case Managers work closely with clients to empower them to achieve housing stability and improve their overall well\-being.

**Primary Responsibilities**

***1\. Client Assessment and Case Planning:***

* Conduct comprehensive assessments of clients' housing needs and barriers.
* Develop individualized housing plans in collaboration with clients.
* Set goals and action steps to address housing challenges and promote stability.

***2\. Resource Referral and Coordination:***

* Connect clients with community resources, social services, and support networks.
* Coordinate referrals for mental health services, substance abuse treatment, and other supportive programs.
* Help clients access financial assistance, food assistance, and other basic needs resources.

***3\. Crisis Intervention and Support:***

* Provide crisis intervention and emotional support to clients in housing crisis situations.
* Recognize early signs of emotional distress, agitation, or conflict
* Maintain a calm and respectful non\-confrontational approach
* Collaborate with other team members and external partners to address immediate housing needs and ensure client safety.

***4\. Documentation and Reporting:***

* Maintain accurate and up\-to\-date client records and case notes.
* Complete required documentation for program reporting and compliance purposes.
* Ensure client confidentiality \& privacy in accordance with agency policies \& regulations.

***5\. Travel and Home Visits:***

* Entering client homes in a respectful, professional, and non\-intrusive manner
* Must have the ability to travel to clients’ place of residence
* Must be comfortable working in person with clients to assist with needs

***5\. Advocacy and Empowerment:***

* Advocate for clients' rights and interests in housing\-related matters as needed.
* Empower clients to self\-advocate and navigate housing systems independently.
* Promote client empowerment and self\-sufficiency through skill\-building and education.

***6\. Budgeting and Analytical Skills:***

* Ability to create and implement client budgets, assist clients in tracking spending and expenses
* Strong organizational and record\-keeping skills

*7\.* ***Confidentiality and Professionalism:*** 

* Knowledge of HIPAA standards and protected health information
* Ability to practice privacy, confidentiality, and record private information safely and securely
* Keep client/case manager privilege in retaining confidential information

**Qualifications:**

***Education:*** Bachelor's degree in Social Work, Psychology, Counseling, or related field preferred.

***Experience:*** Previous experience in case management, social services, or housing advocacy

preferred.

***Skills:***

* Strong interpersonal and communication skills.
* Ability to build rapport and establish trusting relationships with diverse populations.
* Knowledge of housing resources, rental assistance programs, and housing laws/regulations.
* Ability to work collaboratively in a team environment and independently.
* Strong organizational and time management skills.
* Commitment to social justice, equity, and anti\-oppressive practices.
* Proficiency in Google Suite and database management.

* This position may require occasional evening or weekend hours to accommodate client needs.
* Travel within the local community will be necessary for outreach and resource coordination.

* Learns new systems and processes quickly and embraces change.

jobs.description:
**About Waymark**
  

Waymark is a mission\-driven team of healthcare providers, technologists, and builders working to transform care for people with Medicaid benefits. We partner with communities to deliver technology\-enabled, human\-centered support that helps patients stay healthy and thrive. We're designing tools and systems that bring care directly to those who need it most—removing barriers and reimagining what's possible in Medicaid healthcare delivery.

**Our Values**
  

At Waymark, our values are the foundation of how we work, grow, and support one another:
* **Bold Builders**: We tackle the toughest challenges in care delivery by harnessing the power of community and technology.
* **Humble Learners**: We seek feedback, embrace diverse perspectives, and welcome challenges to our assumptions.
* **Experiment to Improve**: We use data to inform decisions and continuously assess our performance.
* **Focused Urgency**: Our mission drives us to act swiftly and relentlessly in pursuit of meaningful results.

If this resonates with you, we invite you to bring your creativity, energy, and curiosity to Waymark.

  

**About this role**

As the Outreach Specialist/California Care Coordinator, Manager for Waymark, you will lead our care coordinators in the market. Reporting to the Market Operations Lead, you will have individual contributor responsibilities as a CC as well as management responsibilities for a team of CCs as the market grows – including helping them implement their day\-to\-day priorities, providing coaching and support around patient interactions, and managing performance to team and individual goals. As a leader in a growing organization, you will also impact how we design, structure, and implement the CC experience for our employees, spanning recruitment, hiring and training, deployment, mentorship, support, resourcing, providing pathways to advancement, and advocating for CCs across our organization.


**Key Responsibilities**
* Provide direct supervision of the day\-to\-day activities of CCs in Sonoma, Orange \& San Bernardino Counties.
* Actively participate in the execution of daily CC tasks alongside team members – such as patient outreach, patient care coordination, and provider communication – serving as a role model and contributing to project deliverables.
* Lead and support CCs with adequate coaching, mentoring, and support to ensure competency and compliance with workflows.
* Work in conjunction with fellow local lead roles and care team members to ensure the seamless execution of cross\-team workflows and projects. The overall care team is multidisciplinary and also includes licensed clinical social workers, pharmacists, and community health workers.
* Review data dashboards to manage CC performance relative to goals and identify strengths and opportunities to ensure goals are met or exceeded.
* Work with the Operations and Learning \& Development teams to hire, train, deploy, and provide ongoing support to local CCs.
* Foster PCP partnerships through communications and either in\-person or virtual meetings.
* Continuously build community partnerships through either in\-person or virtual meetings at community events.
* Maintain knowledge of programs and resources available to community members that may enhance the health care of those individuals.
* Foster an inclusive team environment, encouraging open communication, creativity and knowledge sharing. Contribute as a member of the local leadership team by representing Waymark's values and contributing to a positive and collaborative culture across the local team.
* This role is mainly remote with some in\-person travel required within the market (up to 30%)


**Minimum Qualifications**


* Deep commitment to improving healthcare for underserved populations.History of supervising teams of care coordinators, patient navigators, customer service, outreach specialists or similar roles.
* A leader with cultural and personal humility. Has a strong understanding of Medicaid/MCOs and the barriers to healthcare access and quality among diverse, underserved populations.
* A keen eye for detail and proven track record of effectively monitoring and optimizing metrics, leveraging Excel skills or other tools to analyze data and drive continuous improvement initiatives.
* Demonstrated ability to collaborate and communicate effectively in a multidisciplinary team setting.
* Experience with healthcare data and/or Electronic Health Records.
* A person who thrives on building and supervising a team of care providers, building professionalism and positive culture among those working to support the hardest\-to\-reach patients.
* Ability to travel across your local county to help establish new teams and support existing teams.
* Must reside in one of these counties: Sonoma/Orange/San Bernardino.


**Preferred Qualifications**


* Bachelor's degree in health administration, health management, public health, business administration, or related field.
* Long time resident of one of the 3 identified counties and knowledgeable of MCO and community resources.
* Multilingual skills a plus.


**Hiring Salary Range**



US Employees in Sonoma County \- $93,000 \- $107,000



US Employees in Orange/San Bernardino County \- $85,000 \- $98,000


**In addition to salary, we offer a comprehensive benefits package. Here's what you can expect:**


**Stock Options**: Opportunity to invest in the company's growth.  

**Work\-from\-Home Stipend:** A dedicated stipend for your first year to help set up your home office.  

**Medical, Vision, and Dental Coverage:** Comprehensive plans to keep you and your family healthy.  

**Life Insurance:** Basic life insurance to give you peace of mind.  

**Paid Time Off:** 20 vacation days, accrued over the year, plus 11 paid holidays.  

**Parental Leave:** 16 weeks of paid leave for birthing parents after six months of employment, and 8 weeks of bonding leave for non\-birthing parents.  

**Retirement Saving

jobs.description:
The **Case** **Manager** is responsible for providing confidential, unbiased assistance to eligible Liberty Dental Plan enrollees of State Medicaid programs in need of dental services who also have a co\-morbidity of special health care needs. Responsibilities also include, and are not limited to, assisting the Coordinators Care Management (CCMs) to perform their professional functions.


**Applicants must have a current, valid LVN or LPN license in New York or New Jersey**  



**What You'll Do:*** Inform enrollees of available covered dental benefits.
* **Help to resolve enrollee conflicts and barriers to dental care.**
* Assist in securing enrollee dental services.
* Educate enrollees on their rights and responsibilities.
* Provide enrollees the information on accessing the Liberty vehicles for complaints, appeals or grievance process.
* Ensure enrollee cases and events are documented correctly in the Health Solutions Plus (HSP) database.
* Manage telephone calls and email inquiries not limited to, seeking dental services, dissatisfaction, and second opinions.
* Provide education pertaining to the Liberty Care Coordination Program.
* Provide research and response to various inquiries.
* Compose comprehensive written responses to all applicable inquiries.
* Review and edit, as applicable, all State Agency Provider Network Verification File (PNV) responses prior to submission to Liberty Quality Management.
* Perform Liberty process for enrollees in need of hospital services for dental issues, and delegate such performances to CCM, upon the CCM’s ability to accomplish.
* **Ensure all newly ascertained State Medicaid dental providers are directed to Liberty Provider Relations to insure credentialing.**
* Provide continual Care Coordination communications pertaining to the update and interpretation of state contractual directives for State Medicaid enrollees to the CCM.
* **Perform dental case turnaround time in accordance with access standards regardless of the communication route (e.g., HSP inquiry, workflow, email, facsimile, phone call, etc.).**
* Able to work collaboratively within remote locations.
* Ensure compliance to all regulatory guidelines.
* Comply with all Liberty corporate and department guidelines, policies, and procedures.

Lao Family Community Development, Inc. (LFCD) is a community\-based non\-profit organization established in Richmond, Contra Costa County, California, in 1980\. Since then, LFCD has expanded its operations to Alameda and Sacramento counties with its headquarters located in Oakland, California.

jobs.title: Community Health Worker
jobs.description:
**Improve the health of your community – one person at a time!** First District Health Unit is taking applications for a Community Health Worker (CHW) to provide support services to qualifying local individuals with chronic diseases, or who are at risk. The CHW can help guide clients through the health care and social service systems, provide coaching and education, and identify and address barriers to health. This position is **15 hours per week** at $26\.11/hour. The location is flexible within First District’s seven counties (Bottineau, Burke, McHenry, McLean, Renville, Sheridan and Ward). The Community Health Worker must become certified within 2 years. **To apply, candidates MUST submit a First District Health Unit application at www.fdhu.org, including a resume.**

**Program\-Specific Duties and Responsibilities: Community Health Worker**

* **Preventative Health \& Chronic Condition Support**
* Provide evidence‑based preventative health services to individuals with chronic conditions or those at risk.
* Deliver services strictly within the CHW scope of services, including care coordination, health system navigation, resource coordination, health promotion and coaching, and health education

**Care Plan Implementation**

* Deliver services under a care plan ordered by a licensed physician, PA, RN, APRN, dentist, pharmacist, or psychologist.
* Document all activities in alignment with Medicaid and organizational requirements.

**Client Engagement \& Support**

* Build trusting relationships with clients, families, and caregivers.
* Identify barriers to health (transportation, literacy, housing instability, food access, etc.) as allowed under rulemaking.
* Provide culturally appropriate education and coaching.

**Collaboration \& Communication**

* Work closely with interdisciplinary care teams.
* Communicate client progress, challenges, and needs to supervising clinicians.
* Maintain accurate, timely documentation.

**Requirements:**

* High school diploma or equivalent; additional education in health, human services, or related fields preferred.
* Experience working with diverse populations or individuals with chronic conditions.
* Strong communication, relationship‑building, and problem‑solving skills.
* Ability to work within defined scope of practice and follow care plans ordered by licensed providers.
* Access to a reliable vehicle for traveling in rural North Dakota, valid driver’s license, and auto insurance that covers work travel.
* **Obtain certification as a Community Health Worker** from North Dakota Health and Human Services within 2 years of employment date and maintain active certification and recertification.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Experience in community outreach, health education, or care coordination.
* Knowledge of North Dakota Medicaid programs and community resources.
* Familiarity with rural health challenges, tribal communities, or frontier public health settings.

**Physical Requirements:**

* Work may occur in homes, clinics, community settings, or remotely.

**Job Description**

***A bit about this role:***


The Care Coordinator has an important role supporting TOC Clinical Operations as we ensure our patients have appropriate post discharge planning and follow up in place. The Care Coordinator will support the team with patient outreach and coordination while the patient is inpatient and post discharge.

 ***Your Responsibilities and Impact will include:***

* Reaching out to patients while inpatient to introduce TOC program and communicate post discharge follow up from TOC clinicians
* Scheduling post discharge follow ups (PCP/Specialty)
* Reaching out to hospitals and provider offices to obtain clinical documentation
* Submitting Home Care and DME orders as well as vendor follow up
* Monitoring return fax queue and researching provider profile for updated contact and fax information
* Provide additional operational support for assigned team and manager as designated
* Ensure patients are prepared for telehealth visits by assisting with technology prep
* Collaborate internally in clinical rounds to discuss patients at risk for readmission
* Coordinate lab testing and imaging, and tracking results to ensure that they are reviewed by the ordering clinician
* *This role does not include clinical decision\-making or any activity requiring licensure, and that all clinical tasks are delegated by, and performed under the supervision of, licensed professionals. Clinical Coordinators should direct clinical concerns raised by patients to the appropriately licensed team.]*

***Work Schedule***

* **Schedules Available:** Monday \- Friday 9a\-5:30p ET, 9:30a\-6p ET, 10a\-6:30p ET, 10:30a\-7p ET
* + *Please note, schedules will be discussed during the interview process based on availability. Schedules are selected during time of offer on a first\-come, first\-service basis.*

***Required skills and experience:***

* 2\+ years of patient facing and care coordination experience within healthcare, managed care, home health, and/or community health setting.
* Experience working in a telemedicine environment.
* Fully bilingual (English/Spanish).

***Desired skills and experience:***

* Managed Care / Health Plan experience
* MA Certification (desired), expired MA certifications are OK! \[Verification: A copy of your active or expired certification will be required. No Certification: If you have significant MA experience/background, we may request copies of your MA school diploma and transcripts.]
* Thrive in a fast\-paced, high\-energy, and rapidly growing organization
* Skilled at easing stress and anxiety for patients during difficult times
* Strong communicator, able to effectively interact with various stakeholders including doctors, pharmacies, nurses, and caregivers
* Comfortable working with patients via video, phone, portal
* Entrepreneurial self\-starter who takes initiative and thrives as a collaborative team player
* Quick to adopt and learn new technologies, including electronic health records and various computer platforms (e.g., Google Chrome, Google Sheets)
* Committed to delivering healthcare with the same quality and care you'd want for your own family
* Passionate about helping others improve their health and navigate the healthcare system with compassion, empathy, and warmth
* Highly organized and adaptable, able to manage a large member panel amidst frequent changes

 ***Salary Range:***$23 \-$27 / hour
